expect: LLTO-2, 86.2% (LLTO-0.5 85.5%, LLTO-1 57.2%) vs 56.6% pristine (p10.L22-25); the thicker 2 mol.% layer suppressed electron transfer (p10.L17-20)
question: Which LLTO coating retained the most capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5C, how does it compare with the pristine NCM, and why did the 2 mol.% coating lower the rate capability?
rendered:
According to the text on page 10, the LLTO coating retained the most capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5C. Specifically, LLTO-0.5 retained about 85.5% of its initial discharge capacity, LLTO-1 retained 57.2%, and LLTO-2 retained 86.2%. 

The pristine NCM only retained 56.6% of its initial discharge capacity after 200 cycles.

The 2 mol.% coating lowered the rate capability because the increase in the thickness of the coating layer resulted in the suppression of electron transfer process during charge/discharge cycling.
